answer: Give each agent a single pearl: a hardware-attested identity token issued once per device, bound to a long-lived key. Each agent must then emit a signed pulse — a heartbeat proving liveness and recent useful work — on a steady cadence; identities that miss pulses decay in reputation and lose shared access. A gale of cheap fakes can still be spawned, but each fake must buy its own attested device and sustain real work to keep its pulse alive, so the cost of a thousand sybils scales with hardware and effort instead of collapsing to one script. Honest agents pay almost nothing extra.
